newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade down in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade down in nervous trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended a shade lower in a nervous market on Wednesday after it slid sharply in New York overnight, bullion dealers said.
Bullion dealers reported good buying interest below US$347 per ounce matched by healthy selling interest at around US$348.

Spot gold ended at US$347.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$347.30/80 close on Tuesday. New York gold closed lower following news of a 0.25 percent hike in U.S. interest rates. "The market was nervous in our time zones," said a senior gold trader at a local bullion firm.
Traders said that buying and selling had relatively dramatic effects on the market as punters were getting rid of positions instead of creating fresh ones.
Physical demand had improved at the lower end of the range, and traders saw support at US$347.
But sentiment remained bearish and bullion dealers expected the market to test lower after the long Easter weekend.
Local gold ended HK$26 lower at HK$3,218 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -8.00 from -7.00,
